security_audit.summary: All static findings appear to be false positives caused by Markdown fences, placeholder Cargo metadata, and sample Rust error handling. No prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration, obfuscation, or malicious execution intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Markdown code fences were detected as shell backtick execution.
remediation.suggestion: Keep code blocks clearly marked as examples and avoid language labels or prose that imply automatic execution without user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Sample shell commands create files and modify .gitignore.
remediation.suggestion: State that generated commands should be reviewed before execution in an existing repository.

content.value_statement: Starting a Rust project requires many structural decisions before feature work begins. This skill generates Cargo layouts, module plans, tests, and development configuration for common Rust project types.
actual_capabilities: Creates project structures for Rust binaries, libraries, workspaces, web APIs, and WebAssembly projects.
Provides Cargo.toml examples with dependencies, package metadata, profiles, and workspace settings.
Drafts Rust entry points, CLI parsing modules, error types, and library module exports.
Adds testing, benchmark, examples, README, rustfmt, clippy, and Makefile guidance.
Recommends idiomatic Rust organization for maintainable systems programming projects.
limitations: It provides scaffolding guidance and examples, not a guaranteed complete application.
Dependency versions in examples may need updates for a specific project date.
Generated code requires review for project-specific security, performance, and API needs.
It does not replace running cargo test, clippy, or a security audit on the final project.

use_cases.title: Start a Rust CLI Tool
use_cases.description: Generate a binary project with clap-based commands, configuration modules, error handling, and integration test layout.

use_cases.title: Organize a Multi-Crate Workspace
use_cases.description: Plan a workspace with shared package metadata, core crates, API crates, CLI crates, and integration tests.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap an Axum Service
use_cases.description: Create a web API structure with routes, handlers, services, models, middleware, tracing, and Cargo dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Rust App
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to scaffold a Rust binary project named notes-cli with a simple command structure, tests, and Cargo configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Library Crate
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a Rust library crate for parsing configuration files. Include module layout, error types, tests, examples, and documentation structure.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a Cargo workspace for a service with core, api, cli, and integration-test crates. Explain dependency ownership between crates.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold a Production Web API
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to scaffold an Axum web API with routing, handlers, services, models, middleware, tracing, SQLx, tests, clippy, rustfmt, and release profile settings.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a new Rust CLI that supports init and run commands.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a Cargo binary layout with src/main.rs, cli.rs, command modules, error handling, integration tests, examples, and development commands.

output_examples.input: A team wants to split a Rust product into reusable crates.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes a workspace tree with shared package metadata, crate boundaries, dependency placement, tests, and release build settings.

output_examples.input: A backend engineer needs a Rust API starter using Axum.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines route, handler, service, model, middleware, tracing, CORS, database dependency, and testing structure for the service.

best_practices: Provide the target project type, runtime needs, and deployment context before asking for scaffolding.
Review generated dependencies, editions, and minimum Rust versions against current project policy.
Run formatting, linting, tests, and dependency audits after applying generated scaffolding.
anti_patterns: Do not use the same dependency set for every Rust project type.
Do not execute generated shell commands in an existing repository without reviewing file changes.
Do not treat scaffolded examples as final security or production logic.

faq.question: Does this skill create Rust code or only describe it?
faq.answer: It can generate project structure, Cargo configuration, Rust module examples, tests, and tool configuration for review and use.

faq.question: Can it scaffold both binaries and libraries?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for binary crates, library crates, workspaces, web APIs, and WebAssembly-style projects.

faq.question: Does it choose Rust dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: It suggests common dependencies based on the project type, but users should review versions and features before use.

faq.question: Is the generated project production-ready?
faq.answer: It provides a production-oriented starting point, but the final project still needs review, tests, and security validation.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does this skill perform network access?
faq.answer: No evidence of live network access was found. The only URL is placeholder repository metadata in a sample Cargo file.
